The United Arab Emirates was founded on 2 December 1971, when six of the Trucial States joined in a federation as British protection ended. Ras al-Khaimah joined as the seventh emirate in February 1972.

Britain had announced in 1968 that it would leave the Gulf. Talks to include Bahrain and Qatar failed, and both went their own way. The rulers of Abu Dhabi and Dubai, Zayed and Rashid, made the union work: Zayed became president and Rashid vice-president.

Each emirate keeps its own ruler and much of its own wealth, while Abu Dhabi's oil pays for much of the federation. The UAE has been one of the most stable states in the region.
